newsitem.title: GERMANY: Barenboim conducts cranes to strains of Beethoven.
newsitem.headline: Barenboim conducts cranes to strains of Beethoven.

text.p: Conductor Daniel Barenboim swapped bow tie and tails for a hard hat and overcoat on Saturday to direct an ensemble of 30 building cranes in Berlin to the strains of Beethoven's Ode to Joy.
Barenboim, artistic director of the Berlin State Opera, led a stately "Dance of the Cranes" on Europe's biggest building site, the Potsdamer Platz (Potsdam Square).

The square was once the heart of pre-war Berlin. Now it harbours a vast development where only seven years ago the fortified Cold War border, the Berlin Wall, divided the city's capitalist western and communist eastern halves.

The slow-swinging dance of the cranes was organised to mark the topping out of one of the site's biggest developments, the high-rise headquarters of debis, a subsidiary of industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG.
